issue_context.title: BitArray.CopyTo(Array, int) throws an ArgumentException, if BitArray.Length has been reduced to a multiple of 32
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-collections See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Description BitArray.CopyTo(Array, int) throws an ArgumentException, if BitArray.Length has been reduced to a multiple of 32 ### Reproduction Steps The following code works as expected: ``` using System.Collections; var bitArray = new BitArray(256); bitArray.Length = 33; var intArray = new int[2]; bitArray.CopyTo(intArray, 0); ``` But if the length is further reduced to 32 then an ArgumentException is thrown: ``` using System.Collections; var bitArray = new BitArray(256); bitArray.Length = 32; var intArray = new int[2]; bitArray.CopyTo(intArray, 0); ``` ### Expected behavior The relevant values get copied. ### Actual behavior ArgumentException if BitArray.Length is reduced to a multiple of 32. Reasons seems to be that the length that should be copied is not calculated using the BitArray.Length. Instead the length of the underlying int array is used: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.Collections/src/System/Collections/BitArray.cs#L764 Problem is the underlying int array is not resized when the BitArray.Length is reduced by a small amount (< BitArray._ShrinkThreshold). ### Regression? In .NET 4.8 the length that should be copied is calculated using the BitArray.Length: https://referencesource.microsoft.com/#mscorlib/system/collections/bitarray.cs,370 ### Known Workarounds _No response_ ### Configuration _No response_ ### Other information _No response_

Seems like a bug in this specific branch of the `CopyTo` implementation. Should be using `m_length` instead of `m_array.Length`.

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e86f8d00c62386b4c1b85e8f56be5d63cad5fbb8/src/libraries/System.Collections/src/System/Collections/BitArray.cs#L761-L765

Would you be interested in contributing a PR?

review_comments: Could you convert to a theory where multiple values < 256 are being tested?
I think the only change necessary was to replace `m_array.Length` with `m_length`. Am I missing something?
Yes, m_length is the number of bits stored the `BitArray` represents, so that's why we need to divrem by 32 to get extraBits and quotient (number of full ints)
